title: Excavations in the Atrium of the Church of the Nativity, Bethlehem
author: R. W. Hamilton
location_note: Courtyard (parvis) west of the Church of the Nativity, Bethlehem; no map reference; placed by name.
reading: pp. 1-7 in full; remaining leaves (plates) by keyword
notes: Clearances May-Aug. 1932 during repaving: eastern quadrangle (cloister) walls, upper pavement with 12th-c. and later coins, an earlier lower pavement and colonnade foundation of the primitive atrium. Literary sources (Bernardino Amico 1609, Quaresmius) record three cisterns in the court: cited, not coded separately. Water troughs (mangers) at the foot of the north wall not eligible.

features.subtype: two large cisterns in use in the courtyard
features.quote: Two large cisterns exist in this half of the court

features.subtype: cement-lined, stone-covered channel through the quadrangle walls, probably feeding the eastern cistern; later than the lower pavement
features.period: later than the lower (early) pavement; not otherwise dated
features.quote: A cement-lined and stone- covered channel, which passes through the two walls
